name: Influenza (flu)
seasonality: Winter in temperate regions; year-round in the tropics
description: A contagious respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. Most people recover in about a week, but it can be severe for older adults, young children, pregnant people and those with chronic conditions.
prevention: Get the seasonal flu vaccine
Stay home while you have a fever
Cover coughs and sneezes
Wash hands often
Ask a doctor early about antivirals if you are at higher risk

name: COVID-19
description: A respiratory illness caused by SARS-CoV-2. New variants keep circulating; severity is highest in older adults and people with weakened immune systems.
prevention: Keep COVID-19 vaccination up to date as advised locally
Improve indoor ventilation
Wear a well-fitting mask in crowded indoor spaces during waves
Test and stay away from others while sick

name: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
description: A common respiratory virus that usually causes cold-like symptoms but is a leading cause of bronchiolitis in infants and can be serious in older adults.
prevention: Ask about RSV vaccines for pregnancy and older adults, and antibodies for infants
Keep sick contacts away from young babies
Wash hands and clean shared toys and surfaces

name: Dengue
description: A mosquito-borne viral infection found across tropical and subtropical regions. Most cases are mild, but severe dengue can cause bleeding and shock and needs urgent care.
prevention: Remove standing water around your home
Use insect repellent, especially in the daytime
Wear long sleeves and use screens or nets
Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen if dengue is possible, and see a doctor

name: Chikungunya
description: A mosquito-borne virus causing sudden fever and severe joint pain, which can last for months.
prevention: Remove standing water around your home
Use insect repellent and protective clothing
Check travel vaccine advice for affected areas

name: Malaria
description: A life-threatening parasitic disease spread by Anopheles mosquitoes. It is preventable and curable, but needs fast diagnosis and treatment.
prevention: Sleep under insecticide-treated nets
Take recommended preventive medicine when travelling
Use repellent after dusk
Get tested immediately if you have a fever after being in a malaria area

name: Zika
description: A mosquito-borne infection that is usually mild, but infection during pregnancy can cause serious birth defects.
prevention: Prevent mosquito bites
If pregnant, check travel advice before visiting affected areas
Follow guidance on safer sex after travel to affected areas

nndss: Arboviral diseases, West Nile virus disease
name: West Nile virus
description: Spread by Culex mosquitoes. Most infections cause no symptoms, but a small share develop serious neurological illness.
prevention: Use repellent at dusk and dawn
Wear long sleeves outdoors
Empty standing water

name: Cholera
seasonality: Linked to floods, conflict and unsafe water
description: An acute diarrhoeal infection from contaminated water or food. It can kill within hours without treatment, but oral rehydration works well.
prevention: Drink boiled or treated water
Wash hands with soap
Eat food that is cooked and hot
Start oral rehydration solution at once and seek care for severe diarrhoea

name: Typhoid fever
description: A bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water, causing prolonged fever and needing antibiotic treatment.
prevention: Get vaccinated if you live in or travel to affected areas
Drink safe water
Wash hands before eating

name: Hepatitis A
seasonality: Year-round; outbreaks linked to food and water
description: A vaccine-preventable liver infection spread by contaminated food, water or close contact.
prevention: Get the hepatitis A vaccine
Wash hands after using the toilet and before eating
Avoid untreated water

name: Norovirus
description: A very contagious stomach virus and the leading cause of vomiting and diarrhoea outbreaks in closed settings such as ships, schools and care homes.
prevention: Wash hands with soap, since alcohol gel works poorly on norovirus
Clean surfaces with a bleach-based product
Do not prepare food for others until 2 days after symptoms stop

name: Measles
seasonality: Late winter and spring; outbreaks follow vaccination gaps
description: One of the most contagious viruses known. It can cause pneumonia and brain swelling, and two doses of vaccine give strong protection.
prevention: Check that you and your children have two MMR doses
Call ahead before visiting a clinic if you suspect measles
Isolate until 4 days after the rash starts

name: Mpox
description: A viral illness that causes a painful rash and swollen lymph nodes, spread mainly through close physical contact.
prevention: Avoid skin-to-skin contact with anyone who has a rash
Ask about vaccination if you are at higher risk
Isolate and cover sores until they have fully healed

name: Avian influenza (bird flu)
description: Influenza viruses that spread mainly among birds and sometimes dairy cattle. Human cases are rare and mostly follow animal contact, but can be severe.
transmission: contact with infected birds or animals
prevention: Avoid sick or dead birds and animals
Do not drink raw milk
Wear protective gear if you work with poultry or cattle

name: Ebola
description: A rare, severe viral haemorrhagic fever spread through contact with the body fluids of infected people or animals.
prevention: Avoid contact with body fluids of sick people in affected areas
Follow safe burial guidance
Seek care immediately and report recent travel if symptoms appear

name: Marburg virus disease
description: A rare and often fatal viral haemorrhagic fever related to Ebola, linked to fruit bats and spread by body fluids.
prevention: Avoid caves and mines with fruit bats in affected areas
Avoid contact with body fluids of sick people
Seek care immediately and report recent travel

name: Nipah virus
seasonality: Often December to May in South Asia
description: A rare but very dangerous virus from fruit bats and pigs that can cause brain inflammation, with recurring outbreaks in South Asia.
transmission: contaminated date palm sap or fruit
prevention: Do not drink raw date palm sap
Wash and peel fruit, and discard fruit with bite marks
Avoid close contact with patients in affected areas

name: Lassa fever
description: A viral haemorrhagic illness in West Africa spread by rodents, with Nigeria reporting cases every year.
prevention: Store food in rodent-proof containers
Keep homes clean and free of rodents
Seek early care, since early treatment improves survival

name: Yellow fever
seasonality: Rainy seasons in Africa and South America
description: A mosquito-borne viral disease that can cause jaundice and bleeding. One vaccine dose gives long-lasting protection.
prevention: Get vaccinated before visiting risk areas
Use repellent and protective clothing

name: Polio
description: A vaccine-preventable virus that can cause permanent paralysis. It remains targeted for global eradication.
prevention: Complete the polio vaccination schedule
Check booster advice before travel
Practise good sanitation and hand hygiene

name: Whooping cough (pertussis)
description: A very contagious bacterial infection causing violent coughing fits. It is most dangerous for babies.
prevention: Get vaccinated during each pregnancy to protect newborns
Keep childhood vaccines and adult boosters up to date
Keep coughing people away from young babies

name: Mycoplasma pneumonia
description: A bacterial lung infection, often called walking pneumonia, that is common in school-age children and young adults.
prevention: Cover coughs and wash hands
Stay home while coughing heavily
See a doctor for a persistent cough with fever

name: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV)
description: A common respiratory virus similar to RSV. It can be more serious in babies, older adults and people with weakened immune systems.
prevention: Wash hands often
Avoid close contact when sick
Clean shared surfaces

name: Group A strep
gdelt: ("strep A" OR "group A strep" OR "scarlet fever" OR "strep throat")
keywords: strep a\b|group a strep|scarlet fever|strep throat
description: Bacteria that cause strep throat and scarlet fever, and rarely severe invasive infections. Antibiotics treat it effectively.
prevention: Wash hands and do not share cups
Finish prescribed antibiotics
Seek urgent care for fast-worsening pain, swelling or breathing trouble

name: Meningococcal meningitis
seasonality: Dry season in the African meningitis belt
description: An infection of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord. Bacterial meningitis is a medical emergency.
prevention: Keep meningococcal vaccines up to date
Get emergency care for fever with a stiff neck or a rash that does not fade when pressed

name: Legionnaires' disease
description: A severe pneumonia caught by breathing water droplets from contaminated systems such as cooling towers, hot tubs and building plumbing.
prevention: Keep hot tubs and building water systems maintained
See a doctor quickly if pneumonia symptoms follow a hotel, spa or hospital stay

name: Lyme disease
description: A bacterial infection from black-legged tick bites. Early antibiotics usually lead to full recovery.
prevention: Use repellent and stay on clear paths in tick areas
Check your body for ticks after being outdoors
Remove ticks promptly with fine tweezers
